text: A gentleman, knowing that I am a friend of that one who is collecting materials for Bay Ganyo, handed me the enclosed letter to deliver to him. This letter is so original and characteristic that it would not be a bad idea to print it in the newspaper *Zname* as a feuilleton. How the letter came into the gentleman’s hands — I do not know.
To the editor of the newspaper “It’s Not the Time.”

Ah, you blockhead, why did you denounce me in the newspaper “It’s Not the Time” as if I were supposedly in the opposition, huh? Is that all the sense you’ve got? Does old Bay Ganyo ever become opposition, boy? Or what did you say to yourself: let’s wait till there are fewer of us so we can divide up more. You’re not stupid, I know you. But you’re still stupid, let me tell you the plain truth. That is to say, you’re not stupid, just a bit green. For such matters, ask your foreman. You, so to speak, got hold of the bone yesterday, while your uncle has been gnawing at it for nine years now and has no intention of letting it go anytime soon. And do you know, boy, let me tell you straight: there’s enough for you, there’s enough for me. Long live the native land. When I was still going to Sofia, as a deputation to beg that hanged man not to resign, even then — do you remember, at the Vrazhdebna inns? — even then I understood that being in the opposition is no profit. But you’ll say, why? Why indeed? Very simple: because you’ll be standing behind the broom while others weave their little basket. And what people! All top-notch heroes, all educated, polished. The previous ones of ours were downright wild. They stole openly, by force, clumsily, and even allowed themselves some gallantries, compromising honor with women, girls, and... Ah, boy, is that how it was? And in the end they fell into the trap with both feet. Look, today’s ones are not like that. There’s no gallantry in them. That is — how should I put it — not that there isn’t any, but who’s going to climb up to Djendem Tepe, to Nebet Tepe, who’s going to rummage around the baths asking what happened. And who needs it anyway. As for business dealings, they’re good at them. The truth is the truth! They got down to business in such a way that, shame or no shame, I’ll confess to you, brother, I was stunned too. Bravo, you scoundrels! Just look what a thing science is. To deal with such people — now that I understand. The previous ones of ours had taken the path of violence, killing here, hanging there, shooting there, they had ruined the whole lot. And why? — For nothing. And today, look at that? They only won’t let you move during elections, and for everything else — freedom! Shout, curse, strain yourself as much as you like — nobody says a thing to you. And why should they push the opposition — let it make all the noise it wants, who listens to it. Our people just twirl their mustaches and snicker at them. Power is in their hands — they don’t want to know anything. And now, when so many railways are to be built, so many companies formed, so many ports constructed, you’ve just now found the time to denounce me as if I were supposedly in the opposition. Don’t do that, brother. Was our friendship really that far? Are you jealous of me, or what? For, supposedly, haven’t you struck it richer than I have. Just do the math, how many places do you get money from. And I — what? I mind my little trade, and that’s that. And after all, you know these things happen by agreement. If you help me get into some juicier enterprise too, do you think I wouldn’t repay you for it? I know how things are done. And not only that, but you, devil that you are, have twisted the letter so that, when a person reads it, he’ll even think I’m against the Personage. Me? Do you take me for such a disloyal man? Didn’t we supposedly give our word that it’s not the time? I’d understand if power weren’t in our hands, if we were sniffing from the sidelines — then the hell with it, you’d blacken and go on as before, together with the Personage. But now, when we’ve got hold of the bone with both hands and when it’s just the time to secure ourselves for old age, am I to go and say some plain word about the Personage? Old Bay Ganyo is no fool; he knows when it’s time to shout “long live”! One “long live” — hop, one enterprise. And when its time comes — we know how to shout something else too. That’s how the world goes. If nothing else, at least that philosophy we’ve understood to the bottom, the blasted thing.

Boy, have our folks perhaps gone a bit too far with the Lomchans? I hear: wounded, killed! Well, we’d better keep our wits about us, indeed... they cut off that one’s hands, so that his time might not come upside down...
Enough for now. Long live His Royal Highness!

Do you see how I’m shouting “Long live!”, and yet you’ve gone and said that I was against it. You’re jealous of me, may the devil take you. You know well that if we start shouting over each other, no one knows who will shout louder. And if it comes to showing respect, I still won’t give in. You will kiss a hand, I — both hands; you will kiss a lap, I — the feet; you will kiss somewhere else, I — somewhere even more elsewhere. So are you going to compete with me, eh, you blind fool?
